title: Nazca Lines made to be seen from the sky

tellings.quote: They only make sense 150 to 500 m in the air, which is far higher than any of the closest vantage points on the ground.

plain: The Nazca Lines, huge figures and lines drawn into the desert ground in southern Peru, are said to make sense only when seen from the air. Michels says this himself, without naming a source: the figures "only make sense 150 to 500 m in the air, which is far higher than any of the closest vantage points on the ground." He raises it because it would suggest whoever made them meant them to be seen from the sky.
